Hello Vincent,

Their aren't any special installation considerations for installing on a headless server without X11.
You just go ahead and complete a regular command-line based install of Revolution R Open - see: http://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/documents/rro/installation/
If you do install it on a headless server, your R users won't have interactive graphics capabilities and will
need to output their graphics to graphic files.

Is this machine connected to the internet?  If not, another consideration will be how your R users will install packages.
In that case, you will want to setup your own internal R package mirror.

Revolution R Open 3.2.0 includes:
The latest R engine, R 3.2.0. This includes many improvements <http://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/news/#r320>, including faster processing, reduced memory usage, support for bigger in-memory objects, and an improved byte compiler.
Multi-threaded math processing <http://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/rro/#intelmkl1>, reducing the time for some numerical operations on multi-core systems.
A focus on reproducibility <http://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/rro/#reproducibility>, with access to a fixed CRAN snapshot taken on May 1, 2015. Many new and updated packages are available since the previous release of RRO -- see the latest Package Spotlight <http://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/spotlight/> for details. CRAN packages released since May 1 can be easily (and reproducibly!) accessed with the checkpoint function <http://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/documents/rro/reproducibility/#timemachine>.
Binary downloads for Windows, Mac and Linux systems <http://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/documents/rro/installation/#sysreq>.
100% compatibility <http://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/rro/#compatible> with R 3.2.0, RStudio and all other R-based applications.

You can download Revolution R Open now from the link below, and we welcome comments, suggestions and other discussion on the RRO Google Group <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/rropen>. If you're new to Revolution R Open, here are some tips to get started <http://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/documents/getting-started/>, and there are many data sources you can explore with RRO <http://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/documents/data/>. Thanks go as always to the contributors to the R Project <http://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/documents/what-is-r/#contributors> upon which RRO is built.

Enjoy!

# David Smith

Hi Paolo,

This issue is due to the fact that for most R users, including yourself, the default library path points to your user folder instead of RRO. The MKL installer was expecting it to point to RRO.

To get MKL working on your system:

1. Please remove the file you copied and uninstall MKL. This way we'll start with a clean slate.

2. Reset the library path for the current session, type:
    .libPaths("C:/Program Files/RRO/R-3.2.0/library")

(Tip: To make this change permanently you'd have to put this in your C:/Program Files/R-3.2.0/etc/Rprofile.site)

3. Install MKL again.

Let me know if that fixes the issue for you.

Josée
